result:
**Round 76: PASS. `browserVerified` and `realVerified` are both true, and I found no bugs.** Clips now snap to markers in every case the task asked for, and I ran every real-browser row at 1440x900 and 1280x720.

I tested with Playwright Chromium in a new anonymous context on `/studio-lab`, using real mouse drags. I placed the markers at 6.300 s and 14.700 s instead of the task's example 12.3/20.7, because only about 19 s of timeline fits on screen at 1280. Both are off the grid, so a result of x.300 or x.700 can only come from a marker. Results were the same at both viewports:

| Row | Result |
|---|---|
| **Move** | A clip dragged to 3 px past the marker lands at 6.300. A drag that ends nearer a grid line lands on the grid line (6.000). |
| **Clip end** | A clip whose end is dragged near 14.7 ends at 14.700. |
| **Cross-lane move** | To both music and stems: the move ghost shows 6.300 during the drag, and the clip lands there. |
| **Trim** | A right trim ends at 14.700 with source offset 0. A left trim starts at 6.300 with source offset 1.300. I read the offset from the detail panel and status text, not from the audio. |
| **Group move** | The first clip (the one dragged) lands at 6.300; the second keeps its 3 s offset. |
| **Library drop** | The drop ghost and the dropped clip land at 6.300. A drop whose end falls near 14.7 lands its end there. The video lane still refuses audio, unchanged. |
| **Snap off / Alt** | Snap off and Snap on + Alt both give a free 6.375. Snap off + Alt snaps to 6.300. |
| **Undo/Redo** | The markers' ids, times and names are identical before the move, after it, after Undo and after Redo. Undo and Redo each take one step. |
| **Real audio** | Playing from the marker with the clip on it: the meter rises to 0 dB about 79 ms after the double-click. After Undo, playing from the same marker gives silence for 1.3 s while the playhead keeps moving. |
| **Neighbours** | With a marker present, a nearer clip edge still wins. On a fresh load with no markers, results match round 75. Marker drag, the marker right-click menu and "Play from here" still work. No hydration or console errors. |
| **Security** | Anonymous `/studio/middle-east` shows "Sign in required" and no workspace. The token API returns 401 for anonymous requests. The page sent no token, download or R2 requests and no Authorization header. |
| **Source unchanged** | HEAD, A's file hashes, the 451 frozen files and the 4 protected files all match at the start and end of my run. |

- **Blocked:** the fake-Bearer check returns 500 because the backend isn't available in the cloud. It is not counted as a pass or as a failure of A's work.
- **Gate:** the full test suite, typecheck, build, Biome, `npm run verify` and the e2e smoke test are left to the root gate. A's 8 targeted test files passed (201 tests).
- **Budget:** at 1440 the audio check needed three invalid attempts before the valid one. That is one more than the "two extra attempts" the policy allows. All three were my test-script mistakes, not app failures:
  - Undo reversed the Mute click instead of the clip move.
  - Space didn't stop playback while the marker had focus.
  - With only one short clip, the project ended at 3 s, so playback wouldn't start at 6.3.

  The first half of the check gave the same result in every attempt. At 1280 the first attempt was valid.

**For B (observations, not bugs):**
- **A's group-move note:** if the nearest snap target is a marker the group can't reach, the group falls back to the grid line, even when a reachable clip edge is closer. That follows the contract, but it's B's call whether to keep it. I didn't test it in the browser.
- **Solo/Mute in undo history:** Solo and Mute clicks are undo steps, so Undo after toggling Mute reverses the Mute, not an earlier edit. This was already the case before this round.
- **Playing past the project end:** double-clicking a marker that lies past the end of the project does nothing and shows no message. This was also already the case before this round.

On the Ableton side, the move result matches the Live 12 manual (§6.7) and the Alt result matches §6.10. Trim is only inferred from the manual's wording. Group move, library drop and the nearest-wins rule aren't stated there, so they remain unconfirmed.

Everything is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`. The report is `c-round-76.md`, the results are in `c-round-76.json`, and scripts, screenshots, meter traces and test output are in `c-round-76/`.
